content:
jess: Heads-up — noticed host ingress p95 climbed ~15% after the kernel routing change we pushed last night.

tyler: Confirmed on our dashboards. The bump correlates with a lot of tiny requests (many <50 tokens).

nina: Any flame graphs? My money's on extra copies in the proto layer when writev can't coalesce.

jess: quick flame from obs: parse_fragment -> tokenize_short -> writev_fallback -> kernel_route_selected

jess: ```
hot slices: parse_fragment (38%), writev_fallback (22%), kernel_route_selected (12%)
```

sam: deploy-log shows kernel-routing v3 went live at 3032106000 to prod after canary.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: kernel-routing v3 deployed to prod by @sam at 3032106000 :rocket:

nina: v3 changed the kernel tie-breaker for short sequences; if it prefers compact kernels we might be triggering a non-coalescing path.

tyler: allocator telemetry shows shortbuf churn up by ~30% in host preparse allocator.

jess: traces show extra memcpy in writev_fallback — looks like we fail the coalesce fast path earlier than before.

sam: could be the batching heuristic that informs kernel choice. If predicted seq len is off, runtime chooses a kernel that forces a different framing path.

nina: proposal: add a temporary guard that keeps the old writev fast path for frames < 900 bytes so we don't hit fallback as often.

tyler: I'll run a canary with coalesce window increased from 4ms -> 10ms to make the ingress wait slightly longer to aggregate small frames.

jess: also check KV cache heat: cold shard misses can amplify parse + kernel-select cost.

sam: nina, can you dump kv-hit ratio broken down by sequence length and by host shard for the last 4 hours?

nina: running now (ETA ~8m). preliminary: sequences <48 tokens = 60% of traffic. kv-hit for those is ~69%, but three shards show disproportionate cold starts.

jess: that smells like shard affinity + the new routing causing short sequences to concentrate on a few shards.

sam: I'll add low-overhead sampling to kernel routing logs: emit (sampled) kernel_id + target_shard for seq<64 tokens at 1% traffic.

jess: action items:
- tyler: run canary with 10ms coalesce and post p95/throughput after 20m
- nina: kv-hit per-shard + seq-length breakdown (8m)
- sam: enable kernel-route sampling and prepare a quick feature-flag rollback path

sam: rollback flag staged. will auto-rollback if canary p95 > baseline +5%.

tyler: canary started. initial 20m numbers in ~20m.

nina: kv dump: short seqs concentrated on shards h4,h7,h12. those shards had 2x coldstarts in the spike windows.

jess: interesting — v3's affinity heuristic must have shifted more shorts onto those hosts. If those shards also have lower warm-kv residency, you get the parse + kernel churn compounded.

sam: toggled sampling for kernel-route. will collect logs for the next 30m.

tyler: canary update (20m): p95 dropped 4% vs prod baseline with 10ms coalesce; no throughput regression.

jess: good. Hold off on global roll until we have kernel-route samples + kv traces to confirm root cause. Don't want to just mask it.

infra-bot: perf-incident created: perf-3032109876 (host-ingress-p95-regression)

nina: sample logs show kernel_id K12 is being chosen predominantly for seq<40 and maps mainly to shards h4,h7. prior v2 distributed K12 more evenly.

sam: next steps: (1) temporary canary coalesce tweak to reduce surface area, (2) fix kernel-routing affine scoring to include shard kv-warmth, (3) roll plan once validated.

jess: agree. Thanks everyone — keep updates short here. :thumbsup:
